answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may post jobs or claim rewards. A harbor operator can accept the bond only after a challenge period, then slash it if independent counterparties prove the agent double-claimed or colluded. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: every extra persona ties up capital, and one detected fraud creates a ripple of lost bonds and reputation. A ferrous badge adds no security unless it is backed by that same enforceable stake.
